LinkedIn post by James Fitts, Operating Partner | Executive Operations Lea..., posted 2d ago.

Starbucks is making an interesting bet right now.

After six consecutive quarters of declining comparable sales, traffic is moving in the other direction.

In Q3 FY2026, Starbucks reported:

• North America comparable sales: +8.1%
• North America transactions: +4.5%
• U.S. comparable sales: +7.9%

Those are encouraging numbers.

But what interests me is what Starbucks is investing in to get there.

Under Brian Niccol, the company has invested heavily in store labor, operations and the customer experience as part of its “Back to Starbucks” strategy.

Niccol recently said:

“We have more work to do, but we’re relentlessly focused on reclaiming the third place and becoming the world’s greatest customer service company.”

That phrase “reclaiming the third place” stood out to me.

For Starbucks, the “third place” has historically been the place outside of home and work where people meet, connect, work or simply spend time.

That’s an interesting challenge for a brand that has also spent years becoming increasingly convenience-driven through drive-thru, mobile ordering and delivery.

Now Starbucks is trying to do both: maintain the convenience today’s customer expects while rebuilding the coffeehouse experience and human connection that helped differentiate the brand.

And there is a financial tradeoff to that investment.

North America operating margin was:

Q3 FY2024: 21.0%
Q3 FY2025: 13.3%
Q3 FY2026: 13.6%
